discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (twistronics)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and unconventional superconductivity
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene layers to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so interactions dominate. Jarillo-Herrero's group (Nature 2018) realised this by a simple but bold fabrication trick, tear-and-stack assembly with controlled twist, and found correlated insulating states and gate-tunable superconductivity in pure carbon. This single experiment created a new field: a clean, electrostatically tunable platform in which strongly correlated and superconducting phases, orbital magnetism, Chern insulators and later fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moire systems can be switched on and off in one device. Hundreds of laboratories worldwide have reproduced and extended it, and the twist angle is now a standard design parameter for van der Waals heterostructures. It exemplifies how a new material degree of freedom makes long-standing questions about high-temperature superconductivity experimentally testable.
